provisions.says: Goods must be of satisfactory quality.
Goods that fail to conform within six months beginning with the day they were delivered are taken not to have conformed on delivery, unless shown otherwise.
Rejecting goods ends the contract and entitles the consumer to a refund.
The short-term right to reject lasts until the end of 30 days beginning with the first day after delivery (and ownership or possession passing).
The consumer may require the trader to repair or replace the goods.
After one repair or one replacement fails, the consumer may require a price reduction or use the final right to reject.
No deduction for use may be made from the refund if the final right to reject is used within the first six months (motor vehicles excepted).
A service must be performed with reasonable care and skill.
The consumer may require the trader to perform the service again.
If repeat performance is impossible or not done in a reasonable time, the consumer may require a price reduction.

provisions.cite: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, reg. 29
provisions.says: A consumer may cancel a distance contract within the cancellation period without giving a reason.

provisions.cite: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, reg. 30(3)
provisions.says: For goods, the cancellation period ends at the end of 14 days after the day the goods come into the consumer's physical possession.

provisions.cite: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, reg. 34
provisions.says: On cancellation the trader must refund the consumer, including the standard delivery charge.
The card issuer is jointly liable for the supplier's breach where a single item's cash price is over £100 and not more than £30,000 (s. 75(3)(b)).
A claim founded on simple contract must be brought within six years from the date the cause of action accrued.
